Oklar orsak Även polisen larmades till platsen, berättar RLC-befäl Johan Marklund. – Båda personerna som verkar ha färdats i lastbilen var vakna och talbara. Den info jag fått är att ambulansen har lämnat utan att lasta någon så det verkar ha gått bra under omständigheterna, säger han. Det är ännu okänt vad som kan ha orsakat olyckan. Kalmar bortaslog Degerfors med 2–1 i det allsvenska ångestmötet och klättrar upp på säker mark i tabellen. – Sjukt skönt. Bara att få göra mål är extra bra för det här laget, säger Vilmer Tyrén till SVT Sport. Efter sju matchers måltorka bröts Kalmars förbannelse direkt på Stora Valla. Gästerna rivstartade och gjorde mål redan i den tredje minuten, efter att hemmalagets Daniel Sundgren slagit bort bollen. – Jag sätter laget i skiten efter bara några minuter. Vi lockar dem till en bra press och i det momentet är vi inte tillräckligt skickliga, dels jag men även lagkamrater, säger Sundgren. Det var Marius Söderbäck som därefter fick läget att göra 1-0 och Vilmer Tyrén kunde snart utöka till 2-0 för Kalmar. Men halvvägs in i halvleken blev det en scenförändring. Degerfors hade två ribbträffar och en boll i stolpen innan Nahom Netabay till slut reducerade strax före pausvilan. Netabay: ”Vi spelade som juniorer” – Vi spelade som juniorer första 20. De fick mycket övertag där i början och sedan försöker vi återhämta oss. Men vi hade behövt 2–2 före paus när vi hade tryck, säger en besviken Nahom Netabay till SVT Sport. Den andra halvleken blev mållös trots att Kalmar hade flera vassa lägen. Degerfors-målvakten Matvei Igonen stod för ett par kvalificerade räddningar och Kalmar hade också ett par frilägen där försvararna i sista stund hann emellan. – Vi är bra framåt och borde ha gjort fler än två mål i dag. Vi fick grymt bra energi i starten, första 25 är grymma, säger Vilmer Tyrén. Säsongens första bortaseger Kalmar var inför matchen seriens sämsta bortalag med bara två poäng på 12 matcher. Det här var deras första bortaseger för säsongen. – Det var mycket som klickade i dag. Det var på tiden men det viktigaste var tre poäng, konstaterar Carl Gustafsson. Lagen byter nu plats i tabellen och Kalmar går upp på säker mark med 22 poäng, två före Degerfors på kvalplats. Nästjumbon Örgryte har 18. – Det är tufft just nu, det tar jättehårt. sources.summary: En man i 35-årsåldern utan vapenlicens, boende i Vimmerby kommun, hade gevär, pistoler, revolvrar och en kulspruta hemma i sin bostad och i en lagerlokal. Nu misstänks han för flera brott. – Det är ett av de större vapenbeslagen som gjorts i Sverige, säger åklagare Jacob Semark.

Foto: Polisen Stort vapentillslag – hittade 31 vapen hos man Uppdaterad igår 18:36 Publicerad igår 18:09 En man i 35-årsåldern utan vapenlicens, boende i Vimmerby kommun, hade gevär, pistoler, revolvrar och en kulspruta hemma i sin bostad och i en lagerlokal. Nu misstänks han för flera brott. – Det är ett av de större vapenbeslagen som gjorts i Sverige, säger åklagare Jacob Semark. Mannen greps den 30 december 2025 och har suttit häktad sedan i januari tidigare i år. Det var när civila poliser fattade misstankar om att mannen var narkotikapåverkad och kunde ha narkotika i sin bostad som en husrannsakan genomfördes och vapnen hittades. Flera av dem var fungerande skjutvapen. – Han har sagt att han fått vapnen och föremålen av släktingar, säger Jacob Semark, åklagaren i fallet. Vad säger du om den förklaringen? – Jag kan inte ge någon förklaring på varför han hade vapnen, mer än att det kanske är som han säger, men han får ändå inte ha vapnen. Han har ingen vapenlicens. Mängder av nazistföremål i bostaden På bilder i förundersökningsprotokollet syns även stora mängder nazistföremål i mannens bostad, bland annat en byst av Hitler, flera nazistiska flaggor och nazistuniformer. Det finns även bilder och videor på när han heilar, uttalar nazistiska slagord och poserar med SS-flaggor. – Det har vi givetvis tittat på, men utredningen har inte kunnat ge något svar på syftet, men han säger själv att han är intresserad av andra världskriget, säger Jacob Semark. Är han nazist? – Det kan jag inte säga att man kan belägga, men han har ett intresse för det. Har ni utrett om han är del av något kriminellt nätverk? – Såvitt vi har kunnat, men det verkar inte som att han är det. Mannen själv förnekar att han är nazist och säger i förhör att det handlar om ”en skämtjargong” och satir. Nekar till brott Förutom olika vapen hittades även ett hölje till en bomb, elva pyrotekniska pjäser, tolv tårgasfacklor, signalpatroner och flera stubintrådar. Nu åtalas mannen för synnerligen grovt vapenbrott, brott mot vapenlagen, brott mot lagen om brandfarliga och explosiva varor och ringa narkotikabrott. Han nekar till brott. Årets nomineringar till Augustpriset är här, och listan innehåller allt från ungdomskärlek till tankar om döden och en studie av fiskars inre tankeliv. 18 litterära verk har chans att tilldelas Augustpriset. Idag tillkännagavs årets nominerade i kategorierna Årets svenska skönlitterära bok, Årets fackbok och Årets barn- och ungdomsbok. De sex titlar som nominerats till det Lilla Augustpriset presenterades. – Det här är alltid en jättepirrig dag, säger Mikaela Zabrodsky, VD för Svenska Förläggareföreningen som delar ut Augustpriset. Kanske kan det bli i år som han går från nominerad till vinnare. Den hyllade romanen Ultravåld lös med sin frånvaro när Tone Schunnesson blev utan nominering. sources.text: Image source, Reuters Image caption, Monfils and Svitolina played in the mixed doubles together at this year's US Open and reached the semi-finals By Jack Burgess Published 19 October 2026 Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina has announced the end of her marriage with French former tennis player GaÃ«l Monfils, citing the emotional impact of the war in her country. The 32-year-old, who is ranked number six in the world, wrote in a heartfelt post on Instagram about the effect the conflict and "what the war has done to me inside". "This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," she wrote, saying "I need to find my way back to myself". Svitolina said she felt she could not do that within her marriage. She said her husband Monfils, 40, "listened" and "respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget". "Some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you," the four-time Grand Slam semi-finalist wrote. It was "the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love", Svitolina said. "Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me," Svitolina, who grew up in Odesa, said. Ukraine's Black Sea port city has been heavily bombed by Russia throughout the war. Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. "What you didn't see were the sleepless nights, the doubts, and the feeling of slowly losing myself." The tennis power couple married in 2021 and have one child together - a four-year-old daughter called Skai. Svitolina said her daughter "will always come first", adding "our marriage is ending, but our family is not". Monfils, a former world number six, was expected to play the final tournament of his career at next month's Paris Masters in an emotional farewell. However, the two-time Grand Slam semi-finalist's retirement was effectively confirmed last week when he appeared on the International Tennis Integrity Authority's list of retired players. Once a player removes themselves from anti-doping protocols, they are not eligible to compete in professional tournaments. Monfils, who won 13 titles on the ATP Tour, is preparing to start a new career in finance after joining a Swiss wealth management firm. sources.title: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 50 security recruits, local authorities say
sources.summary: Three missiles hit a camp in government-controlled Shabwa province that officials say was being used as a training centre for new recruits.
sources.text: Image source, AFP Image caption, Yemen's government said the missile strike killed recruits to its internal security forces (file photo) By David Gritten Published 19 October 2026 More than 50 security personnel have been killed and 200 injured in a Houthi missile strike on a camp in Yemen's central province of Shabwa, local authorities say. A spokesman for the Saudi-backed Yemeni armed forces said the Iran-backed group launched three ballistic missiles at al-Alam camp near Ataq city, which was being used as a training centre for recruits to the security forces and police. The head of Yemen's Presidential Leadership Council, Rashad al-Alimi, condemned what he called the "criminal attack" and promised a "firm response". The Houthis' military spokesman said they had targeted "Saudi enemy concentrations". Yemen's devastating civil war has flared up in recent months. At the start of October, pro-government forces launched a major offensive that aims to retake territory in western Yemen that is controlled by the Houthis. With air support from a Saudi-led coalition of Arab states, they managed to regain control of territory on the Red Sea coast that overlooks the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, which the Houthis captured in a surprise assault in September. However, fierce fighting is continuing there, as well as around the besieged government-controlled city of Taiz, and to the north in Marib and al-Jawf provinces. The Houthis have also responded to the Saudi air strikes by launching missiles and drones at airports, energy facilities and military bases in neighbouring Saudi Arabia. Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says Published 4 days ago On Yemen's desert battlefield, a war with global consequences is being waged Published 12 October 'We are terrified but we want to get an education', say Yemeni schoolgirls Published 6 October Monday's attack in Shabwa is one of the deadliest reported since the start of the escalation. Shabwa province's media office said in a statement that ballistic missiles struck the Martyr Ahmed al-Sulaimani Training Centre, where recruits from several provinces were undergoing training to be members of the internal security forces. According to a preliminary assessment, 53 were killed and more than 200 injured, it added. A video posted on social media appeared to show several bodies scattered across the ground. Shabwa's deputy governor, Fahad al-Khalifi, told AFP news agency that hospitals in the province were overwhelmed and had been forced to transfer the most seriously wounded to neighbouring Hadramout and Aden, where the government is based. Some of them were in a critical condition, he said. Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani said the attack constituted a war crime because the internal security forces training centre was not a military target. He also accused the Houthis of "attempting to fabricate a false media victory, boost the morale of its collapsing elements, and cover up the defeats and setbacks it is suffering across various combat axes". The Houthis' military spokesman, Yahya Sarea, said in a statement that the missiles targeted a gathering of "Saudi enemy" forces at al-Alam camp, which he said was run by Saudi officers. There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities. In a separate development, Houthi-run media reported that a Saudi air strike on a home in the Sahar district of the Houthi-controlled northern province of Saada on Sunday killed at least 10 people and injured 23 others, many of them women and children. According to the Houthi-run health ministry in north-western Yemen, a total of 141 people had been killed in Saudi strikes over the past seven weeks. The government's health ministry, meanwhile, said last week that at least 1,282 people had been killed in the conflict across Yemen since 6 August. In Saudi Arabia, at least 19 people have been killed in Houthi attacks targeting the kingdom's airports since the beginning of October. Yemen has been devastated by a civil war that began in 2014, when the Houthis ousted the government from the capital, Sanaa. The conflict escalated in 2015, after the Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to restore the government's rule. A four-year-old informal ceasefire began to unravel in July, when the Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea. The Houthis said they were retaliating for what they call a Saudi blockade of their territory, as well as an air strike on Sanaa airport that they blamed on the kingdom. sources.title: Italy plans tougher security measures after violent protests
sources.summary: The government crackdown comes after protests over rising costs broke out into violent clashes.
sources.text: Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images Image caption, More than 200 people were arrested across the weekend, according to Italian media By Hafsa Khalil Published 19 October 2026 Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is poised to approve emergency security measures, according to local media, after protests over rising costs broke out into violent clashes in Milan. The measures include extending preventative detention to minors and restricting group gatherings, Milanese paper Corriere della Sera reported. Police deployed tear gas and water cannons after protesters - many in masks - threw paving stones, bins and chairs at officers over the weekend. More than 250 people were detained, 80% of whom were minors, Italian police said. The expected crackdown comes after Meloni chaired an emergency security meeting on Monday afternoon. No official announcements have been made. More than 5,000 people gathered in Milan over the weekend. As well as clashes between police and some protesters, stores were looted and property was set on fire. High-end shops in the city's centre closed early on Monday, with many boarding up their windows over fears of further damage. Measures to crack down on youth gangs are expected to be approved as early as Tuesday as part of a decree law, according to Corriere della Sera. Local media reports suggest social media was used to invite young people to Italy's squares over the weekend. Rioting and violence have broken out on the sidelines of mostly peaceful youth-led protests in other European countries including France, Spain and Albania, in recent weeks. Milanese Mayor Giuseppe Sala said he was worried this represented a "new phenomenon" that "originates from an international scenario and therefore feeds itself". Speaking to Ansa, he said he witnessed "smashed shop windows, looted stores, and frightened citizens", adding that "what happened here is what we are seeing in many cities around the world". Of the 271 people taken to police stations on Sunday, 32 were arrested, including 23 minors, police said on Monday. A further 28 people were reported to judicial authorities. Italian media reported that people - including police officers - were injured. Violence between protesters and police also spread to other cities in the north. Meloni said people in Turin were detained while "carrying cobblestones and window-breaking hammers", while a train station in Bologna was closed as a precaution after similar disorder. "To demonstrate is a right. To lay our cities to waste is not," Meloni said on Saturday, adding that "hooligans" had exploited the protests to "sow chaos". The prime minister - who is facing an election next year - also called on her political opponents to condemn the rioting. "Do not be ambiguous about this," she said in a post on X, explaining that condemnation must be "unanimous" because "any hesitation becomes justification". Democratic Party leader Elly Schlein said her party had always condemned violence and that the rioting should not be used to stifle the voices of peaceful protesters across the country who are struggling to make a living, Ansa reported. The violent disorder followed anti-government protests held by students in various Italian cities on Friday, and echoed similar unrest in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands took to the streets. När den hedervärda frågan om att kandidera till riksdagen kom var det svårt att svara något annat än ja. Jag gjorde det, med reservation för att jag visste att jag behövde få känna efter ordentligt en tid till. Ingen ”nytändning” – Men nytändningen har inte riktigt infunnit sig. Kanske sitter sviterna av många år i politiken kvar? Jag tror att året med över 30 skjutningar satte djupa spår. Jag har aldrig känt samma glädje till politiken igen efter det. Jimmy Jansson säger i sitt inlägg att han fått upp ögonen för ”livet utanför politiken”. Men exakt vad han tänker göra nämner han inte. Han har dock redan flera uppdrag utanför politiken. Bland annat tillträdde han som vd för OK detaljhandel AB för bara några dagar sedan, enligt uppgifter från Bolagsverket. Dessutom driver han eget företag och har flera styrelseuppdrag. Åsa Kullgren, även hon S-politiker från Eskilstuna, tar nu över Jimmy Jansson roll i riksdagen. På onsdag ska hon infinna sig i riksdagen. – Det var någon på Socialdemokraternas kansli som ringde och berättade det i morse. Hur känns det att nu bli riksdagsledamot? – Det är blandade känslor.
